text:
Jesper Wallstedt is the best goalie story in the league right now, and the numbers back the headlines. He is 16-2-3 with a .925 save percentage, and he has stopped 19.1 more goals than the shots he faced would usually allow (goals saved above expected, our measure of a goalie against the difficulty of his workload). That sits in the 94th percentile, and the NHL just named him its second star of the week.

What makes it convincing is where he is winning. On high-danger shots he is at .800 against a league .687, and he is beating the average on medium-danger chances by even more: 10.85 goals saved there alone. Michael Russo of The Athletic wrote that "Jesper Wallstedt draws Carey Price comparison" after the overtime win in Montreal.

The honest caveat is size. Last season he was a solid +5.8 over 35 games, and our talent range still pegs his true save rate closer to .900 than .925. Twenty-one starts is a hot start, not a settled level. But the Wild have built their season on him, and right now he looks like the reason they believe.
headline: The Wall of St. Paul, again
